rationale: A wins because it does the boring adult thing: it builds four usable reporter lanes from the facts it actually has. A's "Mercury says it's profitable on 200,000 businesses. Consumer banking will test that claim" is a clean economics angle with the missing proof named. B's "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones" is punchier, but it smuggles in a thesis the update did not give it. That is how you get a founder excited and a reporter annoyed.
gaps_in_A: "Mercury wants to hold consumers' money without being a bank" is slightly loose. The update says partner banks provide the banking services; the safer version is about the bank-partnership structure, disclosures, and who legally holds deposits.

"the crisis-era winner converting its moment into a bigger ambition" pushes beyond the supplied facts. Mercury became well known after SVB; the update does not prove it was a winner in growth, deposits, or customer acquisition.

"A consumer-fintech reporter at a fintech trade outlet or the banking desk of a business publication" is good but still a little broad. The strongest shapes are consumer banking competition, fintech-bank partnerships, and fintech economics.
gaps_in_B: "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones" is the big foul. The update says Mercury is profitable and entering consumer banking; it does not say consumer neobanks were broken or unprofitable.
"now wants your paycheck" invents direct-deposit behavior. Checking and savings do not automatically equal paycheck capture, and that distinction matters.

"the first time the SVB-era customer base is being asked to bring their personal money too" invents targeting. The facts say invite-only waitlist, not that existing Mercury business customers get invites or are being asked to convert.

"the same arrangement that has been the live question in fintech-banking supervision" adds an outside regulatory peg not supplied in the update. Maybe true in the world, but this judging task asked for grounding in the provided facts.
